experiment: Token context for early display: an LSTM token LM combined with partial audio in the gate, in token choice, on the display, and as a long-context decoder branch
motivation: The 20M transducer picks tokens from the encoder frame and the last two BPE pieces only. In emit_early_v1 the display gate stays 32-66ms (dev-clean) behind its oracle and every delay-penalized model loses WER. The question is whether token context, combined with the audio that has already arrived, closes either gap.
lm: LSTM over the 500 BPE pieces (embedding 512, 2 x 768), trained on the 960h transcripts plus the LibriSpeech LM corpus; dev and test text unused

designs.A_gate: LM features of each preview token (log-probability, LM top probability, first-choice flag) added to the display gate; recognizer unchanged
designs.B_choice: When the transducer emits in a preview pass, the token is the best non-blank one under log p + lam * LM log p; the transducer alone decides when to emit. lamn applies the same rule to the native pass, which changes the final output
designs.C_completion: The display also shows the LM's greedy continuation (whole words) of what a pass displays while its joint probability is at least tau
designs.D_branch: Architecture change: an LSTM over the whole token history, initialised from the LM, is added to the 2-token decoder output through a zero-initialised projection; fine-tuned with the delay penalty
designs.E_branch_frozen: D with the LSTM frozen; only the projection and the original model train

hypotheses.H1: A lowers the R1 delay of the gated display against the same gate without LM features, by at least a third of the gap to the oracle, on the penalty-0.005 model
hypotheses.H2: B lowers the rewrites of ungated previews by at least 20% relative and lowers the R1 delay
hypotheses.H3: B on the native pass lowers the full-dev WER of the penalty-0.005 model (paired interval excludes zero)
hypotheses.H4: C lowers the R1 delay by at least 10ms at the same rewrite target
hypotheses.H5: D loses less WER than the matched baseline without the branch at the same penalty (paired interval on dev-other excludes zero) at no more lag
hypotheses.H6: E does not beat D; if E matches D, the gain comes from LM knowledge rather than from added trainable capacity

training_arms: 960h, SpecAugment, lr 0.0005 with linear decay to 10%, 160/320ms training chunks, averaged weights, 240 minutes on a V100: baseline and D at penalties 0.005 and 0.01, E at 0.005. Branch parameters use AdamW (projection lr 0.001, LSTM lr 0.0001)
evaluation: As in emit_early_v1: eight zero-fill previews per 320ms chunk, hold display, gate fitted on 800 dev utterances and thresholds (gate and tau) chosen on 300 others, delay and rewrites on the fixed 200 + 200 subset, WER on all of dev-clean and dev-other with a paired utterance bootstrap; every encoder pass charged 5.0ms, LM steps not charged; test unused
compute: USC CARC Discovery, one GPU per job
added_before_any_result: 2026-11-23, after the 4-minute smoke run and before any result: a baseline and a D arm without delay penalty (same recipe, 240 minutes). H7: without a penalty D has a lower full-dev WER than its matched baseline. This separates what the long context does for accuracy from what it does under a penalty.
added_after_A_B_C_results: 2026-11-23, exploratory, after the A/B/C results were seen: native-pass fusion weights 0.1, 0.15 and 0.35 on the two delay-penalized checkpoints (full-dev WER only), and paired bootstraps of every fused result against the same checkpoint without fusion. The weight is not selected on held-out data; the whole sweep is reported. Also: native-pass fusion at weight 0.15 on every arm trained here (baselines and D/E), with paired bootstraps against the same arm without fusion, to see whether the trained branch and the external LM give the same gain or add up; and paired bootstraps of each D/E arm against its matched baseline.
added_after_D_E_results: 2026-11-23, exploratory, after the D/E results were seen. D after 240 minutes has the lag and WER of the 480-minute baselines of emit_early_v1 (same recipe, twice the training time), so its advantage over the 240-minute baselines may be faster convergence rather than a better trade-off. Three D arms at 480 minutes (penalties 0.005, 0.0075, 0.01) are compared with r4_dp005_sc_decay, r4_dp0075_sc_decay and r4_dp010_sc_decay (paired bootstrap on full dev, same gate code). H8: at 480 minutes D still has at least 10ms less word delay without previews than its matched baseline, at a full-dev WER that is not higher (the paired interval does not lie above zero), at every penalty. If not, the 240-minute advantage is convergence speed.
